claims.text: A machine-learned interatomic potential can serve as a better thermodynamic-integration reference than a conventional EAM for multicomponent HEAs near melting.
Standard EAM potentials miss many-body atomic configurations present in ab initio HEA liquids.
The proposed method applies to both solid and liquid equiatomic or near-equiatomic HEAs such as CoCrFeMnNi.
The MLP should be trained on ab initio data spanning a broad range of configurations, including liquid configurations.
The applicable temperature interval is approximately Tm minus 200 K to Tm plus 50 K.
Liquid polymorphism and configurational complexity are pronounced in the specified temperature interval.
An MLP has greater flexibility than an EAM for representing local atomic environments and many-body interactions.
The enhanced representational flexibility of an MLP improves phase-space sampling.
Continuous interpolation over complex configurations reduces phase-space mismatch between the reference potential and the ab initio target.
MLPs trained on appropriate solid and liquid data can accurately reproduce ab initio forces and energies in both phases.
Reproducing ab initio forces and energies gives the MLP reference closer phase-space overlap with the ab initio system than an EAM reference.
Closer reference-target phase-space overlap reduces the effective thermodynamic-integration path length.
A shorter effective thermodynamic-integration path lowers integration errors.
The MLP reference is expected to reduce thermodynamic-integration path mismatch by roughly 30–50% relative to TOR-TILD EAM references.
The reduced path mismatch should produce more accurate free energies for both solid and liquid HEA phases.
TOR-TILD uses traditional EAM references as the relevant baseline for HEA thermodynamic integration.
Analogous improvements have been observed in simpler elemental or binary systems.
The effectiveness of the MLP depends on the quality and configuration range of its ab initio training data.
